catalog_quote: In UT there are two verb classes that consistently condition allomorphy in suffixes that immediately attach to them: Class I conditions lenis allomorphs and Class II conditions fortis allomorphs. Also verbs of class I condition allomorphy depending on whether or not the verb root bears primary stress. There is no way to predict which class a verb belongs to based on its phonological form: verbs in both classes may be of 2, 3, and 4 syllables in length, and may bear stress on any of these syllables, and may end with the same inventory of vowels. ... (19) Class 1 Verb roots that do not keep primary stress sawí-me ‘getting well/aliviando’ witá-me ‘defecating/defencando’ otó-me ‘taking/tomando’ (20) Class 1 Verb roots that do keep primary stress ayó-me ‘being angry/estando enojado’ ripí-me ‘staying/quedándose’ ropóca-me ‘bending down (human)/agachandose’ (21) Class 2 elowí-me ‘being hungry/…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding quotations are verbatim in copies we hold at the stated places (Valdez Jara 2013 sec. 2.4 pp. 23-24 and p. 144; Burgess 1984 p. 7, verified on the page image since the SIL scan has no text layer). Languoid identity is right: Valdez Jara places Urique under Ethnologue Western Tarahumara [tac]; Burgess's data are Rocoroibo/Guazapares, the same lect (Burgess 1984 p. 5). (2) The classification lexical rests on two independent first-hand descriptions: a 2013 dissertation (morphosyntax-focused, but explicit that root stress is unpredictable from phonological form and lexically patterned, with lexical root classes governing stress retention under suffixation) and the 1984 SIL sketch ('phonemic' word stress, no placement rule). sources.quote: Describes Choguita Rarámuri (Central, different glottocode) as lexical stress within an initial three-syllable window; for Western Tarahumara it only lists Burgess 1970/1984 and Burgess & Merino Mares 2001 as the descriptions and makes no statement about WT stress placement. Its bibliography supplied full citations for the WT wishlist items.
sources.locator: sec. 1.3 printed p. 12 (prior work: 'Western Rarámuri (Burgess 1970, Burgess 1984, Burgess & Merino Mares 2001, inter alia), which differs significantly from Northern and Central varieties'); sec. 3.1 printed p. 65 (three-syllable stress window in Choguita; 'window-like restrictions on stress placement are described across Rarámuri varieties (including Brambila's (1953) description of Norogachi Rarámuri and Morales Moreno's (2016) description of Rochéachi Rarámuri)')
